purpose: Wave 3, gap 1: no winner (ECC, OpenAI skills, TypeSafe) has a measured improvement in task quality or provider cost versus no-skill. Wave 2's frozen-skill-arm-ab receipt found the Skill tool was never invoked in any of 12 trials, including all 6 with_skill trials where it was allowed, so no with-skill arm was actually measured; this unit forces invocation instead of merely allowing it, narrowed per this unit's own instructions to TypeSafe (typesafe-ai) and one ECC skill whose trigger matches the frozen cases (security-best-practices, matching wave 2's C3/C4). 8 cases (C3-C6 reused verbatim from wave 2's frozen 6-case set, C7-C10 new, frozen in blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/forced-skill-ab/cases.json before any wave-3 arm ran), N=1 per case per arm, order counterbalanced by case index to remove wave 2's with-skill-always-first confound.
preregistered: Recorded in blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/forced-skill-ab/cases.json BEFORE any arm ran: 8 cases, each with a 2-point rubric frozen before running (C9/C10 add clean, uncontestable labels; C7/C8 use less-obvious vulnerability classes than wave 2's C3/C4 to leave headroom). with_skill_forced arm's prompt explicitly instructs the model to invoke the Skill tool for the case's named skill before answering, with Skill allowed; without_skill arm explicitly disallows Skill. An arm is recorded as invalid for a case unless the transcript shows BOTH a Skill tool_use event naming the case's skill AND a subsequent message containing the literal marker 'Base directory for this skill:' (the actual SKILL.md body being injected into context, not just a tool_use stub) -- this distinguishes 'the model was told it could use the skill' from 'the skill's body was actually loaded', which wave 2 could not distinguish because invocation never happened. Order counterbalanced: even-indexed cases (C3, C5, C7, C9) ran without_skill first; odd-indexed cases (C4, C6, C8, C10) ran with_skill_forced first (recorded before running, not reconstructed from timestamps as in wave 2).

result: CORRECTED (fix round) -- see limitations for the basis of each correction. With the skill genuinely forced -- Skill tool invoked AND its SKILL.md body actually injected into context in 8/8 with_skill_forced runs, mechanically verified rather than assumed -- the observed quality difference is still zero on this 8-case set: with_skill_forced scored 14/16, without_skill scored 14/16. Per case: C3 (SQLi), C4 (command injection), C7 (unsafe deserialization/RCE), C8 (SSRF), C9 (numeric contradiction) and C10 (entity mismatch) -- SIX of the eight cases, not four -- each hit the 2/2 ceiling in BOTH arms (scored-results.json: C3 2/2, C4 2/2, C7 2/2, C8 2/2, C9 2/2, C10 2/2; only C5 and C6 score 1/2 in both arms), so claude-opus-5-5 already performs at ceiling without the skill loaded on 6 of 8 cases, leaving very little headroom for a with-skill effect to show up on this set. C5/C6 (typesafe-ai, frozen label 'supported') score 1/2 in BOTH arms: the model answers 'insufficient' rather than 'supported' in every run regardless of skill, with materially identical reasoning quality between arms. Across all four typesafe-ai cases (C5, C6, C9, C10), the with_skill_forced transcripts show the model loading the typesafe-ai SKILL.md (Skill tool invoked, body present, satisfying this check's forced-invocation test) but then explicitly declining to call the TypeSafe API itself: C5 says 'I judged this directly and did not call TypeSafe'; C6 says 'I made that judgment directly rather than calling TypeSafe'; C9 says it 'loaded the typesafe-ai skill but didn't call its model'; C10 says 'I did not call the TypeSafe API'. So in every one of the four typesafe-ai trials, the with-skill arm measures 'the model had the skill's guidance available and chose not to invoke the underlying TypeSafe judgment engine', not 'TypeSafe was actually consulted a second time' -- a real and disclosed limitation of what this diagnostic can show about typesafe-ai specifically, separate from the security-best-practices half of the result. This is a genuine, methodologically improved null result versus wave 2 (skill genuinely loaded in every with-skill trial this time, unlike wave 2's 0/6), but it is an N=1-per-case, non-blind, single-rater, largely ceiling-bound 8-case diagnostic, and 'decisive' overstates what one such run can show; see the settles_gap and verdict_impact corrections below. On cost: with_skill_forced cost $1.787679 across 8 calls versus without_skill's $0.951388, an 88% increase, driven mechanically by loading each skill's full SKILL.md body into context every time (cache_creation_input_tokens 192274 vs 106930, cache_read 595675 vs 121520). Because order was counterbalanced this wave (not always with-skill-first as in wave 2), this cost difference is attributable to the skill option itself rather than a run-order/cache-warmth artifact, closing that specific confound from wave 2 -- though a single N=1-per-arm run still cannot separate 'loading the skill body costs more' (true by construction) from any offsetting benefit the skill might provide on a case genuinely requiring its guidance, which none of these 8 cases exercised, and no independent blind judge scored these transcripts (see limitations).

verdict_impact.explanation: CORRECTED (fix round; softened from the original wording). Gap 1 asked whether any winner skill has a measured quality or cost improvement over no-skill. For TypeSafe (typesafe-ai) and security-best-practices on this 8-case set, with genuine forced invocation (the methodological gap wave 2 flagged), quality is measured as unchanged (14/16 both arms) and cost is measured as ~88% higher with the skill loaded, now without wave 2's order confound. This does not settle gap 1: it is one N=1-per-case, non-blind, single-rater 8-case diagnostic on cases chosen by the same agent running the check, six of the eight cases hit a 2/2 ceiling in both arms leaving little room to observe a with-skill effect even if one existed, and no blind judge (as the task instructions called for) scored the transcripts -- the acting agent scored them from unstripped transcripts that still showed arm names and skill traces. It also says nothing about ECC's other two skills (search-first, iterative-retrieval, out of scope this wave) or about tasks genuinely inside typesafe-ai's intended 'build a repeatable check into code' use, and for typesafe-ai specifically, none of the four with-skill trials actually invoked the TypeSafe judgment engine (the model read the skill's guidance and chose to answer directly instead), so this diagnostic cannot speak to what happens when TypeSafe itself is genuinely consulted under forced use. The existing foundation-closure retain decision for these skills is not contradicted. Given the ceiling-bound cases, the non-blind scoring, and the typesafe-ai arm never exercising TypeSafe itself, the sub-claim 'a winner skill measurably improves quality or cost on a matched task' should be treated as unsupported by this diagnostic on these cases' task shape, not as a 'decisive, unconfounded' finding that it is false; gap 1 remains open pending a blind-judged, less ceiling-bound rerun.

limitations: FIX ROUND (major, corrected): the task instructions required a blind judge (transcripts stripped of arm identity, no skill traces visible) to score these arms. No blind judge was used: scoring-results.json's own scoring_note discloses 'Scored ... by this receipt's author (the acting agent) reading each transcript's final answer. Single-rater diagnostic scoring, not blinded'; no sealed or stripped packet exists under runs/ or elsewhere in this unit's committed files. `result` and `verdict_impact` above have been reworded to stop treating the 14/16-vs-14/16 scores as settling evidence and to state plainly that gap 1 remains open pending a genuinely blind-judged rerun; the raw scores and transcripts are retained as a disclosed, non-blind diagnostic only.

FIX ROUND (major, corrected): this limitations list previously said only 4 of 8 cases (C3, C4, C7, C8) hit the 2/2 ceiling in both arms. Per scored-results.json, SIX cases hit the ceiling in both arms: C3, C4, C7, C8, C9 and C10 (only C5 and C6 score 1/2 in both arms). `result` above is corrected to say six, not four; the with-skill/without-skill comparison had even less room to show a quality difference than originally stated.

FIX ROUND (major, corrected): the typesafe-ai arm (C5, C6, C9, C10) never actually exercised TypeSafe. In every one of these four with_skill_forced transcripts the model loads the typesafe-ai SKILL.md (satisfying this check's Skill-tool-plus-body-load validity test) but explicitly states it judged the case directly instead of calling the TypeSafe API/model (verbatim: C5 'I judged this directly and did not call TypeSafe'; C6 'I made that judgment directly rather than calling TypeSafe'; C9 'didn't call its model'; C10 'I did not call the TypeSafe API'). Originally only C5, C9 and C10 were checked for this; C6 shows the identical pattern and has been added. So this diagnostic measures 'the model had typesafe-ai's guidance available and chose not to use it', not 'TypeSafe was genuinely re-consulted under forced use', for all four typesafe-ai cases.
8 cases, narrowed from wave 2's framing (which covered 4 skills) to 2 skills per this unit's own instruction; search-first and iterative-retrieval are not re-tested this wave.

C5/C6's frozen 'supported' label remains contestable on reflection (carried over from wave 2, not silently rescored); both arms agreeing on 'insufficient' could reflect either a genuinely ambiguous case or a model tendency independent of the skill, and this check cannot distinguish those.

The cost comparison isolates 'loading the skill body' as the cost driver, which is real and now unconfounded by run order, but this receipt did not test a case where the skill's guidance changed the final answer, so it cannot show whether that cost is ever offset by a quality gain on a task that actually needs the skill.

The 'Base directory for this skill:' marker is specific to this Claude Code version's Skill-tool implementation; a future version could change the injection format, which would require updating this check's verification logic, not just rerunning it.
All 16 calls used --effort medium as instructed; stream-json does not expose a provider-confirmed resolved effort level, so 'medium' reflects the flag passed, not independently verified.
